destination.name: Central Coast
destination.tagline: A semi-rural stretch of beaches, bushland and national parks between Sydney and Newcastle.
destination.description: The Central Coast lies between Sydney and Newcastle and takes about 90 minutes to drive through without traffic. Gosford is the main city, with beach towns at Terrigal, The Entrance and Umina, and national parks at Bouddi, Brisbane Water and Wyrrabalong. The Bouddi Coastal Walk runs 8 km between beaches, and Aboriginal rock engravings can be seen at Bulgandry and in Brisbane Water National Park. Wondabyne, on Mullet Creek, has the only railway station in Australia with no connecting road.
whyVisit: Meet crocodiles and wombats at Australian Reptile Park

goodToKnow.title: Trains from Sydney
goodToKnow.detail: Trains from Sydney Central leave about every 30 minutes for Woy Woy, Gosford, Tuggerah and Wyong, taking 1.5 to 2 hours and costing $5 to $8 one way on an Opal card.

goodToKnow.title: Park fees
goodToKnow.detail: Bouddi and Brisbane Water National Parks charge $8 per vehicle per day, payable by card at pay machines or through the Park'nPay app.

goodToKnow.title: Reptile Park hours
goodToKnow.detail: Australian Reptile Park opens 9 am to 5 pm daily except Christmas Day, with adult tickets about $54 to $59 and a daily crocodile show.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: Visit in {months}: guides suggest spring and autumn for mild weather and thinner crowds than summer, and humpback whales can be seen from The Skillion from May to November.
